title: NotaryFlow — Logged Out, Still In
objective: Sign in, capture your session cookie, log out — then use the captured cookie to access your account again, as if you were never logged out.

verifier.condition: A request using a session token issued by a login succeeds on a protected page after that session's logout request has completed.

weakness: Logout only clears the cookie in the browser's response; the server never revokes the session on its side, so the token itself keeps working if it's replayed.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /logout (clears the cookie client-side only; the token keeps working)
seededData: User alice with a known password. In-memory session store.

credentials.label: User account
credentials.note: Note your session cookie's exact value before logging out.

hints: Capture your session cookie's value before you click log out — write it down somewhere.
After logging out, try sending a request to a protected page using that exact old cookie value, set manually.
Logging out usually clears a cookie in the browser. That doesn't tell you what the server did with the token on its own side.
burpNotes: Log in, copy the Cookie header's value from any authenticated request, log out, then replay a request to the protected page in Repeater with that old cookie value set manually.
